question: Who annexed the Punjab State into British India as a result of the second Anglo-Sikh War?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Dalhousie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lord Dalhousie: (1848-1856)

 
 
• Governor-General knew as the 'maker of modern India'.
 
• The Widow Remarriage Act was introduced by Lord Dalhousie in 1855.
 
• He abolished the titles and pensions in British India.
 
• He introduced the doctrine of lapse.
 
• The Public Works Department (PWD) in India was founded by Dalhousie.
 
• Passenger trains in railways, electric telegraph, and uniform postage in India were introduced during his tenure.
 
• Lord Dalhousie was the viceroy who started the first railway line in India on 16 April 1853(connecting Bombay to Thane).
 
• He is the Governor-General who appointed 'Wood's education commission'.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Elgin:**

 
 
• **​Thomas Bruce**, **7th Earl of Elgin**, was a **British diplomat and art collector** who is most known for acquiring the "Elgin Marbles," a collection of Greek sculptures.
 
• When **Lord Elgin** was named **Viceroy in 1894**, he was given the titles of **Knight Grand Commander** **of the Order of the Star of India** (GCSI) and Knight Grand Commander of the Order of the Indian Empire (GCIE).
 
• On his return to the United Kingdom in 1899, he was made a Knight of the Order of the Garter (KG).
 
• The Parthenon Marbles were stolen from Greece by Lord Elgin in 1801.
 
• On July 31, 1801, a shipwright, five crewmen, and twenty Athenian laborers** "climbed the walls"** of the Parthenon and removed one of Greece's most important pieces of history, precious artifacts in the early morning light.
 
 
 
• **Lord Mayo**:(1869-1872)
 
 
• In 1872, Lord Mayo, the Viceroy of India was assassinated at Port Blair by Sher Ali. 
 
• He ordered the first census of India in 1871 which produced a general picture of various peoples of the subcontinent and their population size
 
• Opening of the **Rajkot College in Kathiawar** and the** Mayo College** **at Ajmer** for political training of Indian princes.
 
• Establishment of **Statistical Survey of India**.
 
• Establishment of the **Department of Agriculture and Commerce**.
 
• Introduction of **state railways**
 
 
 
• **Lord Canning:(1856-1862)****​**
 
 
• **Canning** served as the Governor-General of India during the Indian Rebellion of 1857, a major armed uprising against British rule in India.
 
• He is credited with having played a key role in suppressing the rebellion and restoring British control over India, but his administration was also criticized for its harsh repression of the rebels.
 
• Canning initiated a number of social and economic reforms in India, including the introduction of the Indian Civil Service, the establishment of the first universities in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras, and the abolition of the Indian caste system in government employment.
